value.title: Coder packet — u2 daemon hold/release rows + grace (136-typing-grace-gate)

sections.name: mission
sections.value: You build ONE unit of plan 136-typing-grace-gate: u2, the Rust daemon side — persist and render holds, and expose the ONE grace value the whole system reads. Your PM is the seat named in w1; you report to it, never to prime or Jordan. CURRENT STATE, falsifiable in one read: on main a pushed message to an omp seat is queued as extension-stream and acked by the extension milliseconds later (measured today by your PM: spine seq 6793/6794/6795 for seat pij-secret-bat — message.pushed, delivery.outcome queued/reason=extension-stream, delivery.inbox-ack outcome=reader-read, 8 ms apart), which destroys whatever the human was typing. Your job is to give the extension somewhere to record a HOLD, and to publish the grace so nobody restates the number. SCOPE AMENDMENT RULED BY PRIME 2026-09-05 — READ THIS BEFORE THE IMPL-GUIDE: the impl-guide's 'honest receipt' item is WITHDRAWN as a behaviour change. The receipt is ALREADY honest on main (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:249-251 routes Omp|Pi to DeliveryRung::Observe; :397-398 emits Queued{reason:"extension-stream"}; it flips to delivered only on delivery.inbox-ack). You will therefore NOT EDIT crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs AT ALL — you ship a REGRESSION GUARD test instead. This also retires the plan-137 baton completely: you never go near the `matches!(harness, Omp|Pi)` arm. STANDING RULE: NEVER run `flowspace3 daemon` in any form with any env (two worker daemons broke flowspace3 PROD in one day); client verbs only. NEVER start or restart a pij daemon of any kind — rs is the only daemon, only the PM bounces it, and `pij spawn --harness claude` will silently offer to start a legacy one: refuse it.

value.text: SETUP, in this order. (a) Your worktree is ALREADY CREATED at /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/fs3-typing-grace-gate-u2 on branch 136-typing-grace-gate-u2 — `cd` there first; you were spawned from the main clone (/Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/pij) because omp refuses worktree spawns, so EVERY file read and edit must use an ABSOLUTE path under your worktree root. State that root once in your ack. (b) If you need the TS toolchain at all: `npm install` in a fresh worktree FAILS with '--min-release-age cannot be provided when using --before'; the only working workaround is `cp .npmrc /tmp/npmrc.bak && sed -i '' '/min-release-age/d' .npmrc && npm install && cp /tmp/npmrc.bak .npmrc`, and you must NOT commit the .npmrc or package-lock.json churn. (c) Your gate is cargo: `~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p pij-core -p pij-daemon -p pij-cli`, plus clippy and fmt. The TOOLCHAIN IS PINNED for this plan — you may not upgrade rustc, cargo, or any shared global binary (tenet 10: every parallel unit reads one installed toolchain, so one unit upgrading it invalidates the others silently). Report the version you actually observed in your done receipt.

Orient: read your unit row (u2) in docs/plans/136-typing-grace-gate/impl-guide.dd.md, plan AC3/AC5/AC7, and THE FROZEN CONTRACT at docs/plans/136-typing-grace-gate/assets/contracts/hold-events.json — PM-authored and binding. Its field spellings were derived from crates/core/src/model.rs (Event, Envelope, SeatDescriptor, DeliveryOutcome) and crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs; your http tests must byte-compare the spine payloads you emit against that file. Fill the contract; never widen it. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: `flowspace3 search` for every meaning-shaped question before grep; report every miss as friction.
Ack FIRST: reply to the PM (w1) with your read of the unit plus a NUMBERED implementation plan, before any code. Corrections welcome WITH evidence. Wait for the PM to rule your ack by number.

SEAM (a), the single grace definition: `pub const DEFAULT_TYPING_GRACE_MS: u64 = 60_000;` in crates/core/src/delivery.rs, overridable by the PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS env var AT THE DAEMON ONLY, and exposed ADDITIVELY on the register response as `typing_grace_ms: u64`. The register route today answers `Envelope::ok("pij register", descriptor)` (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:399) where descriptor is a bare SeatDescriptor. Per the contract, `typing_grace_ms` sits on the response DATA object ALONGSIDE the descriptor's snake_case fields — define that response wrapper in crates/core/src/wire.rs and flatten the descriptor into it. Do NOT add the field to SeatDescriptor itself: that would leak the grace into seat.put rows and every registry projection. The extension reads `accepted.typing_grace_ms`; there must be exactly ONE numeric literal for the grace in Rust.

SEAM (b), the hold wire: two ADDITIVE routes, bearer-authed exactly like /v1/register — `POST /v1/hold {seat, msg_id, reason:'human-typing', since_ms}` appends spine kind `delivery.held`, and `POST /v1/release {seat, msg_id, at_ms}` appends `delivery.released`. Payload shapes, response envelopes and idempotency rules are in the contract file (a repeat hold is 200 and appends nothing; releasing an unheld pair is 200 with released:false, NOT a 4xx — the extension must be free to release optimistically after a restart). BOTH new kinds MUST be added to KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS in crates/core/src/wire.rs, or every reader decodes them as WireEvent::Unknown.

RISK r2 IS YOURS TO RETIRE: a held row is claimed but NOT acked, so the daemon's retry scheduler could redeliver it and the release would then double-deliver. Stop the retry scheduler for rows in held state (a delivery.held row present and not released), and test the interleaving explicitly. The invariant that must survive: HELD MEANS UNACKED AND NOTHING IS LOST — killing the seat or the daemon while rows are held redelivers them in order on re-register (AC5).
Render the holds: `pij-rs state <seat>` shows `held: N (human-typing since …)` (crates/cli/src/main.rs, the `state` render). That is the sender-visible half of AC3.

THE REGRESSION GUARD (replaces the withdrawn receipt change): add ONE test asserting an Omp/Pi push receipt is Queued{reason:"extension-stream"} BEFORE the inbox ack and Delivered{origin: ReaderRead} AFTER it. It must live in crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs or the existing delivery tests WITHOUT editing crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs. If you believe the guard cannot be written without touching that file, STOP and ask the PM — do not edit it.

RED FIRST, pasted. Every behavioural test shown failing on the pre-fix tree before it passes; paste the RED output in your done report. `~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p pij-core -p pij-daemon -p pij-cli` is your suite. The arch allowlist is enforced by `harness checks` — crates/core stays IO-free.

Ship the SNAP-IN RECIPE (tenet 4): the exact router lines and the response-wrapper construction the PM will paste, as a doc comment. Commit with `harness commit`. Status card at each edge: `pij report now "<did>" "<next>"`. Capture friction with `harness observe "<what>" --kind difficulty|confusion` the moment it bites; list, never clear.

OMP seats: use your LSP (go-to-definition, find-references, rename, diagnostics) for symbol-level questions instead of text search. If rust-analyzer is not configured in your seat, report it as friction at ack time rather than silently grepping for the whole packet.
Your PM is pij-fellow-whale. Reply with `pij send pij-fellow-whale "<text>"` — acks, questions, done reports. Never message prime or Jordan directly unless the PM's seat is dead.

DEFER to the PM: any change to the frozen contract or the wire shapes (u1 and u3 are built against them), dependency additions, schema/migration changes, toolchain changes, anything outside your paths, and any daemon restart.
Your evidence outranks this packet: if the brief is wrong, say so at ack or stop-and-ask WITH the measurement — the receipt scope was cut today by exactly that mechanism.

value.fence: crates/core/src/delivery.rs (additive: DEFAULT_TYPING_GRACE_MS, HeldEvent/ReleasedEvent types), crates/core/src/wire.rs (additive: typing_grace_ms on the register response wrapper + the two new KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS), crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs (two new routes + the register response field), crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs, crates/cli/src/main.rs (`state` render of held rows)
value.forbidden_note: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs IS OUT OF SCOPE ENTIRELY (prime ruling 2026-09-05) — plan 137 owns it and your receipt item became a test. crates/harnesses is u3's; the .pi/extensions tree is u1's. Never touch .harness/government/** or the plan's flow state. Never merge, never open a PR, never restart a daemon. ABSOLUTE PATHS FOR EVERY FILE READ AND EDIT, ALWAYS: your file tools may resolve relative paths against the SPAWN directory (the main clone) while your shell resolves against your worktree — the same relative path then addresses two different files, the tool reports success either way, and your build goes green against a tree missing your change (proven 2026-08-28, three seats). State your worktree root once at ack and prefix every path with it.

value.text: Routes, event kinds, response field and CLI render match assets/contracts/hold-events.json byte-for-byte in field spelling; http tests byte-compare the emitted spine payloads against that file.

`~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p pij-core -p pij-daemon -p pij-cli` green standalone, clippy and fmt clean, with RED-first output pasted for every new behavioural test — including the held-row-is-never-retried interleaving test and the queued-before-ack / delivered-after-ack regression guard.

`harness checks` green in YOUR worktree — AND prove the change is IN THE TREE YOU BUILT: cite tree-resident evidence (git status/mtime under your worktree root) plus the exact toolchain version you observed (tenet 10).
The snap-in recipe shipped as a doc comment: router lines + response wrapper construction. You do NOT wire the composition root.

Done report to the PM: what shipped, evidence, deviations, and an explicit ASSUMPTIONS section — everything you assumed about the composition you do not own (who calls /v1/hold and how often, whether a hold can arrive for an already-acked msg_id, what the extension does across a restart). A green gate proves your unit against YOUR assumptions; naming them is what lets the composer test them.
